name: Indian Pink
lede: Indian Pink is a soft, warm pink, recorded in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary as first used in 1902, an older entry than most of the other "Indian"-named colors in our library.

sections.title: The oldest of the "Indian" names here
sections.body: The nearest named colors on file are [[rosebloom]], [[rose-dawn]], [[light-congo-pink]] and [[japan-rose]], at 2.8, 3.3, 3.8 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. Neither that dictionary nor our other sources explain what the "Indian" modifier refers to for this particular chip [1]. In Munsell terms it reads 8.7R 7.1/4.7, light and only moderately saturated [1]. 8, 3.3, 3.8 and 4.1 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to this color in 129 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.54 percent, and in 67 by the stricter within-painting measure, which still makes it more common than 53 percent of the named colors we track [2]. Inside those paintings it most often sits as a hidden color, 30 percent of the 67, present without dominating [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.4 times the expected rate, 15 of 721 such paintings, and peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.6 times expected [2].

The earliest match in our archive dates to 1230, in a painting attributed to Berlinghiero, with the latest from 1922, 82 dated paintings in all, 700 years before the name's own earliest record, 1902 [1], a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [1][2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
